tasks.task: YOUR CALL: two fixes that work only on the claims they were built on
tasks.what: From the night's experiment E5. (1) 'A prediction is about a booked fight': a rival camp's boast ('Usman would make him quit', claim-003, three articles) moves from 'predicts his fight' to 'calls him out'. (2) 'A report of what is planned for him is news, not steering': fixes Dana White's 'top two potential opponents' and the reported rematch talks. Both held in two runs and lost nothing, and every training article the key calls a prediction is about a booked fight. But neither moved the validation set, so nothing outside their own claims shows them working. Options: adopt both; adopt neither until a new labelled slice can judge them; adopt only 'booked'. My recommendation: only 'booked', which restates how the key already uses the label.

tasks.task: YOUR CALL: do the three news questions stay tied to the 'what new fact' answer?
tasks.what: Today the code applies the rule ties: 'no fact' makes all three flags no, and a result, next-fight or health fact makes its own flag yes. As the model gives them, 'reports his next fight' is right on 150 training and 35 validation articles; after the ties, 146 and 39. Training prefers the raw flags, validation the ties. Where a flag and the 'what new fact' answer disagree (23 training articles), the flag is right in 11, the fact in 10, both wrong in 2. Options: keep the ties and log every disagreement for review (now); let a confident flag stand against 'no fact'; drop the flags and derive them from the fact. My recommendation: keep the ties and log the disagreements, a cheap list of articles worth a second look.

tasks.task: Design against the two classic failures of grouping one article at a time: stale leader and chaining
tasks.what: Stale leader: a story is described forever by its first article's one sentence (production writes it once and never updates it), so an off sentence misjudges every later article. Suspected cases from the September replay: a story fact that restates June's result for an August article, and a fact about Ilia under a headline about his brother. Chaining: a group grows through its most similar member and drifts; on 2026-08-08 a chain of 0.80, 0.87 and 0.97 walked an Ali Abdelaziz story onto an unrelated matchmaking claim. Production has both sides: the shortlist ranks a story by its closest member, the judge compares against its first sentence.

why.set: Neither failure shows when articles are scored one at a time; only the replay in date order (6.7) can catch them.
why.station: Whether a story's description should be rebuilt from its members as they join (the usual fix for a stale leader) while staying tied to its first fact (the guard against chaining).
why.system: A stale leader posts repeats (G3) or swallows news into the wrong story; a chain swallows news.

tasks.task: After v0: lean grouping toward splitting, and absorb the splits downstream
tasks.what: Your rule (5 Oct, now in goals.md under G3): a story posted twice costs less than a story swallowed. v0's replay leans the wrong way on training: pair precision 0.62 (3 of v0's 38 claims mix two of your stories) against pair recall 0.83 (4 of your 38 split). Levers, each aimed at one side. Against merges: a join needs JEV to be sure (under some confidence, start a new claim instead; the ⚠ joins are the first candidates); a guard that refuses a join when the extracts name a different opponent, event or date; a second look at a claim whose newest article's extract disagrees with its label. Against the cost of splits: the digest writer merges claims that are one story (your idea; it already sees the week's claims together); before a tier-1 post, a check against the last days' posted claims for the same fact (same opponent and event), so a split repeats at most rarely in the loud channel. Two more, to test on the golden replay first, from your first live review (5 Oct, claims #424 and #426: one Instagram statement by Parnasse's camp, reported by three outlets, split across two claims): (1) show the judge each candidate claim by more than its label, for example its first and its latest sentence. #424's label had switched to its one rumour article ('reportedly scheduled', firmer than 'no new fact'), so the third report of the camp's denial was compared with the rumour alone and judged a new story (79% 'none of these', 12% #424), though two denials were already in the claim; (2) make the extract's 'occasion' name the fight or event ('Topuria vs Parnasse, UFC 336'), not where it was said ('Instagram story posted by Chaufourier'): it is part of the text the shortlist compares, so four articles on one fight got four different occasions.

why.set: Pair precision and pair recall on training and validation, and swallowed tier-1 stories counted on their own: the target is none.
why.station: Grouping (6) is where both failures start; 6.9 (stale leader, chaining) is the same family.
why.system: G1 before G3: nothing real is missed, and what repeats is caught by the digest or the post-time check.
